prompt: CHALLENGE: You add 0.3 equivalents of CH₃MgBr to a solution containing BOTH 2-butanone (a ketone) and methyl benzoate (an ester). Which product forms predominantly, and in what ratio?

options.label: Mostly starting material (both carbonyls remain) + ~30% of the Grignard-adducted 2-butanone (tertiary alkoxide, becomes 2-methyl-2-butanol on workup). The ketone is more electrophilic than the ester, so the limited Grignard preferentially attacks the ketone.
Equal amounts of adducts on ketone and ester.
Mostly ester adducted (ester is more reactive).

explanation: Ketones are more electrophilic than esters at the carbonyl C because esters have resonance donation from the -OR oxygen that reduces the δ+ on C. With a limited (0.3 eq) nucleophile, chemoselectivity emerges: the faster-reacting ketone absorbs almost all the Grignard. Great diagnostic question for 'which C=O is more reactive'.
